title: Low-temperature thermal-desorption mass spectroscopy applied to investigate the hydrogen adsorption on porous materials
material_description: (unlabelled 1) | activated carbon from styrene-divinylbenzene (sulfonated with conc. H2SO4, pyrolysed at 1073 K in N2, activated at 1123 K in steam and CO2), provided by TU Bergakademie Freiberg
source_location: main.pdf p.3 (journal p.232), Results text: "2.6 wt% and 2.5 wt% for SWCNTs and activated carbon"
notes: temperature_k left empty and temperature_unstated set only because schema v2 limits temperature_k to 50-500 K: the paper states loading at ~20 K and a heating ramp 20-370 K. Total H2 desorbed in low-temperature TDS (heating 0.1 K/s, spectra recorded to 370 K, all H2 desorbed below 80 K), calibrated with PdH0.7; loaded with 25 mbar H2 at room temperature then cooled to ~20 K (stated temperature approximate; 25 mbar = 0.025 bar), then evacuated (final pressure 1e-7 mbar). Degassing: 470 K (stored as 196.85 C), ~3 h, vacuum better than 1e-5 mbar (stored as 0.001 Pa, a bound). Home-built TDS setup (Fig. 1). Sample mass not stated for this sample (paper: usually <3 mg). Paper says this amount agrees within 0.2 wt% with the maximum 77 K isotherm uptake; not coded as an uncertainty. Reference temperature 370 K is the end of the recorded spectrum. Area: BET 1065 m2/g measured with N2 at 77 K; paper does not say who measured it or on which treatment state of the sample (activated carbon was supplied by TU Freiberg, synthesis details by private communication).
